description: Reference choreography from the @samyzgl TikTok (17.9 s clip, dance content 0.4-13.2 s, then the dancer reaches for the phone and a TikTok end card follows). Trio in a hallway, hand-held camera that pans and ends close to the dancer; main dancer = tracker id 7 (blond, black tee, centre). Move boundaries from the wrist trajectories and motion energy of data/dance/pose/samyzgl_0729aa.npz (see docs/DANCE_MODEL_INTERFACE.md section 4 for the schema).
bpm_estimate_note: Estimated from the fist-to-chin pattern, not from the audio: the 5-switch phrase repeats every 2.81 s (onsets 2.03, 4.90, 7.67, 10.47 s) and the three held switches are 0.67 s apart (autocorrelation peak), which reads as one 4-beat bar at ~85 bpm with the holds on the beat and the two quick switches on roughly half counts. Could equally be 170 bpm in double time.

moves.name: Ready: standing behind the front dancer, screen-left hand resting at the chest, then arms drop
Fist up under the chin with the free arm hanging, head tilts away: screen-right fist, then screen-left, then screen-right, one count each
Quick double switch: screen-left fist to the chin, then screen-right, half a count each
Fist under the chin again, head tilting away: screen-left fist, then screen-right, then screen-left, one count each
Quick double switch: screen-right fist to the chin, then screen-left
Fist under the chin, head tilting away: screen-right fist, then screen-left, then screen-right, one count each
Quick double switch: screen-left fist to the chin, then screen-right
Same fist-under-chin switches while stepping toward the camera: screen-left, then screen-right, then screen-left
Final quick double switch close to the camera: screen-right fist to the chin, then screen-left

notes: Side convention in the names: 'screen-left'/'screen-right' are sides of the video as displayed (it is a mirrored front-camera clip, so the learner who mirrors the screen uses their own left for screen-left). In the npz the detector labelled the screen-left arm 'right_*' and the screen-right arm 'left_*' (xy == xy_raw, no un-mirroring applied), so 'screen-left fist' = right_wrist and 'screen-right fist' = left_wrist.

Each phrase is five fist-to-chin switches: three ~0.65 s holds followed by two ~0.4 s quick ones. The starting side alternates every phrase (screen-right, screen-left, screen-right, screen-left). The raised fist sits just under the chin with the elbow in front of the body, the free arm hangs straight, and the head tilts away from the raised fist.

'ready' is the count-in and starts at the first ok frame (11, 0.367 s; the main dancer has no track in frames 0-10): the judge's reference clock starts count_in_s after the first ok learner frame unless set_ref_clock is used. The front dancer (who starts the recording) walks back during the count-in and occludes the main dancer's screen-right arm until ~2.0 s (left_wrist is NaN before that).
Content ends at 13.15 s: from there the dancer leans in and reaches for the phone (last ok frame 413 = 13.77 s, with a 2-frame tracking gap at 13.57 s); the TikTok end card starts at ~14 s.

Hand-held camera: the hip x position drifts from 0.93 to 0.17 of the frame width over the clip, and from ~10 s the dancer walks toward the camera (nose-to-hip distance grows from 1.2 to 2.4 torso units). Ankles are visible in only ~25% of ok frames (knee-up framing), knees in ~80%.
